findings.text: the UNHELD_ROLES comment (and the measure_dag_order docstring at line 153) records the incident as history -- "Counting it was the measure's first defect: twelve of fourteen reported launches" and "the measure's first reading counted twelve review launches as violations" -- rather than stating the mechanism, so the source carries changelog prose the repository's naming rules ask to state as what the code does.

assert row[drain_measure.WAITS_ONLY_AFTER_FIELD] is True echoes the same flag the fixture set on node_definition at line 47, so it holds for any implementation that copies the field onto the row and does not independently guard the flag's reporting; the contrast test at line 97 is what actually guards the verdict.

assert row["queued_waits"] == [f"{PLAN}#s4"] compares the row's echo of the pointer's own waits list (supplied at line 117) against the value the test passed in, so it moves with the input rather than against an independent source; the violations and edited_wait_launches assertions on lines 121-123 are the anchor.

justifications.durability: the negative control shows the reverted module declaring DISPATCHED_WAITS_FIELD and failing measure_dag_order(..., live_pointers=...) while the head module returns 0 violations on the pointer-omits-edge case and on the flag-true case, and test_two_reads_of_one_window_return_identical_sorted_rows:180 now asserts first["rows"] is non-empty before the sort equality, so the sort has a failing guard.
justifications.evidence: scoped-gate and after_suite-1795385258087802856.log:8 read 65 passed with a closing EXIT=0, baseline_suite-1795385182493442137.log:8 reads 58 passed at the base, and negative-control-repair.log shows the reverted module failing the pointer check outright and reporting the flag row as a violation.
justifications.fit: the module follows the surrounding helper style, but reckon/crew/drain_measure.py:57 and :153 keep incident history in a comment and docstring rather than stating the mechanism, so the fit is not complete.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/drain_measure.py:286-333 reads waits_only_after from the promoted row's node_definition (written by reckon/crew/dispatching/launch.py:397-453 and reckon/crew/node.py:843) and the request's waits through section_waits_for, so an early launch's release record is real rather than invented.
justifications.reuse: the duplicate wait normalisation is gone: reckon/crew/drain_measure.py:311 calls section_waits_for from reckon/crew/admission/wait_refs.py:52, which owns the waits record, and _node_definition reads the ledger field rather than forking reckon/crew/runs.py:343 (which hydrates a pointer's node body from a different key), so no capability is duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside the declared write set, no plan or state file is edited, and nothing outside reckon/crew/drain_measure.py and its test changed; the two declared docs paths are undelivered but are not required by the done_when.
